text:
Mira Patel: Borealis onboarding raised a few items in their security questionnaire. They asked for: encryption at rest + key custody options, SOC2 evidence/timeline, subprocessors list and DPA stance, and embeddings retention/deletion. Copying their bullets below.

Mira Patel: ```
- Do you encrypt customer data at rest? Who holds keys and is BYOK/HSM available?
- Can you provide your SOC2 report or a timeline for completion?
- Please list subprocessors and explain how changes are communicated. Will you accept our DPA edits?
- How long are embeddings retained and can they be deleted on request?
```

Tom Ellis: Short answers for an email: "Yes, data at rest is encrypted. Hosted: cloud KMS (AWS/GCP) with envelope encryption; Dedicated/Private: BYOK supported and HSM-backed options available. SOC2: in progress, Type II expected end of Q3; we can share a readiness pack now under NDA. Subprocessors: published in Trust Center and we provide 30 days' notice for changes; our standard DPA includes a subprocessors appendix. Embeddings: default retention 365 days for hosted, configurable for Dedicated; deletions supported via support ticket."

Sasha Green: Suggested customer-friendly lines: "We enforce role-based access and key rotation for all KMS workflows. For Hosted customers requiring logical separation, we offer dedicated CMKs or BYOK on Dedicated plans."

Ken Wu: I'll prepare the SOC2 readiness pack (control matrix + interim evidence + pentest summary). Tagging Legal for any non-standard DPA redlines.

Mira Patel: Do we have a KMS diagram to attach?

InfraBot: KMS architecture PDF available: /security/diagrams/kms-2026.pdf.

Mira Patel: Great — I'll send Borealis this afternoon with the pack, KMS diagram, and copy Legal on DPA redlines. Will paste the sent message here after I send. :email:
